newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip, tracking U.S. Dow's fall.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip, tracking U.S. Dow's fall.

text.p: Russian shares, tracking a fall in U.S. stock markets on Friday, edged down in modest trade, and dealers said parliament's decision to limit foreign ownership in the national electricity company also pushed prices down.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index lost 3.11 percent to close at 286.03 on $27.84 million in total market volume.
"There are always enough panickers, and Russian blue chips are doing such somersaults these days that now you just want to make some money off of them," said Creditanstalt's Andrei Galperin.

Dealers in Russia's markets, increasingly following moves in world markets, said they watched the Dow Jones industrial average lose more than 50 points in early trading after a strong March jobs report rekindled what some said were expectations of higher U.S. interest rates.
Russian traders also pushed prices down after watching the State Duma lower house of parliament vote to keep 51 percent of UES in state hands and to limit foreign ownership to 25 percent.
President Boris Yeltsin later vetoed the bill.
UES EESR.RTS closed down at $0.1815 from Thursday's close of $0.1910.
Moscow power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS slipped to $1.171 from $1.245 and Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil LKOH.RTS cruised down to $13.35 from $13.82.
Rossiisky Kredit's Oleg Martynenko said the longterm trend was growth but that the market would seek equilibrium near-term.
The RTS index, which hit an all-time high of 349.27 on February 20, has come down steadily since then.
But some dealers said big declines were not in the cards.
"The downward movements are over," Martynenko said. "Over the weekend, everybody will try to grasp what has happened and whether blue chips like Mosnenergo haven't gotten too cheap."
He said Russian players were the most active buyers and that Western investors were still waiting to make sense of the vagaries of the Russian market.
"Most Westerners are sitting and waiting for price or technical signals, or just waiting to see who will buy first."
